classification.difficultyReason: Solve a logistic initial-value problem using supplied partial fractions, then evaluate the solution.

content.prompt:
Solve $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=\dfrac12P\left(1-\dfrac{P}{500}\right)$, $P(0)=50$.

Find $P(t)$ and $P(4)$. Give $P(4)$ to the nearest whole number. Use
$$\frac{500}{P(500-P)}=\frac1P+\frac1{500-P}.$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{dt}{dP}&=\frac{1000}{P(500-P)}\\
\frac{dt}{dP}&=2\left(\frac1P+\frac1{500-P}\right)\\
t&=2\bigl(\ln|P|-\ln|500-P|\bigr)+D\\
\ln\left|\frac{P}{500-P}\right|&=\frac t2-\frac D2\\
\frac{P}{500-P}&=Ae^{t/2}
\end{aligned}$$
Using $P(0)=50$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{50}{450}&=Ae^0\\
A&=\frac19.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{P}{500-P}&=\frac19e^{t/2}\\
9P&=(500-P)e^{t/2}\\
P(9+e^{t/2})&=500e^{t/2}\\
P(t)&=\frac{500}{1+9e^{-t/2}}\\
P(4)&=\frac{500}{1+9e^{-2}}\\
P(4)&\approx225.
\end{aligned}$$
